title: Pollen on a visitor
hook: A flower visitor may leave carrying particles.

knows: Flowers can be visited by insects.
doesNotKnow: Identify a source of pollen that can adhere to a flower visitor.

misconception: Pollen on a bee means the diagram has already shown pollination.
objective: Identify a source of pollen that can adhere to a flower visitor.

claims.text: A flower visitor may leave carrying particles. In this schematic, what sticks to the bee after it brushes a flower’s pollen-bearing anther? The diagram shows pollen moving from an anther onto the visiting bee. A bee can collect or carry pollen on its body. This contact alone does not show pollen reaching a stigma.

The precise supporting passages have not been checked.

claims.text: The stage uses a simplified, not-to-scale schematic and stated model assumptions; it is not a photographic observation of an individual animal.
Recall: A flower visitor brushes a pollen-bearing anther. What may adhere to its body? Pollen can adhere to the visitor after contact with an anther.
